meta.note: Non-UI dependencies mapped across Android, iOS, Flutter and React Native. 'install' is a Gradle group:artifact, a SwiftPM repository URL, 'flutter pub add', 'npm i' or similar; versions are deliberately omitted. Entries with install = null are platform-provided APIs. Status flags (deprecated / archived) were checked against vendor pages and repositories on 2026-11-02.

items.title: HTTP client
items.description: General-purpose HTTP client with interceptors/adapters, retries and request customisation. OkHttp is the de-facto Android engine (Retrofit and Coil sit on it); Alamofire wraps URLSession.

builtin.ios: URLSession (Foundation) - fully capable on its own; async/await APIs built in
builtin.flutter: package:http (flutter pub add http) and dart:io HttpClient
builtin.react_native: fetch() is built into React Native

items.title: Declarative REST API layer
items.description: Describe endpoints as typed interfaces/enums and let the library build requests and decode responses. Retrofit sits on OkHttp; Moya sits on Alamofire.

items.title: Kotlin Multiplatform HTTP client
items.description: Ktor Client is a coroutine-based client with pluggable engines. On Android it runs on OkHttp or CIO; in Kotlin Multiplatform shared code the Darwin engine runs it on iOS. Relevant only if you share Kotlin code with iOS.

ios.name: Ktor Client (Darwin engine, via Kotlin Multiplatform)

items.title: WebSocket client
items.description: Persistent bidirectional connections. Android and iOS ship client APIs; Flutter and React Native each have a thin wrapper or built-in.

builtin.ios: URLSessionWebSocketTask is part of Foundation (iOS 13+)

items.title: GraphQL client
items.description: Typed GraphQL clients with normalised caching. Apollo ships maintained SDKs for Android (Kotlin), iOS (Swift) and JavaScript.

items.title: gRPC client
items.description: Protobuf-based RPC. Official gRPC libraries exist for Android (Java/Kotlin), Swift and Dart; React Native has no first-party gRPC client (Connect-style HTTP clients are the usual route).

items.title: Network reachability / connectivity
items.description: Observe whether the device has a usable network and which transport (Wi-Fi, cellular) is active. Platform APIs on Android and iOS; plugins wrap them for Flutter and React Native.

builtin.android: ConnectivityManager is part of the platform SDK
builtin.ios: Network framework is part of the platform SDK

items.title: JSON serialization (typed models)
items.description: Map JSON to typed models. kotlinx.serialization uses a compiler plugin (no runtime reflection); Codable is compiler-synthesised; json_serializable generates code via build_runner. Moshi (codegen via KSP) is a long-standing Android alternative. React Native has no typed-model layer - JSON.parse yields plain objects (add a validator such as zod if you need runtime checks).

flutter.name: json_serializable
flutter.install: flutter pub add json_annotation dev:json_serializable dev:build_runner

builtin.ios: Codable, JSONEncoder and JSONDecoder are built in

items.title: Reflection-based / dynamic JSON
items.description: Gson maps JSON via reflection. Its README states it is in maintenance mode and not recommended for Android because reflection conflicts with R8 shrinking; prefer kotlinx.serialization (or Moshi) on new code. SwiftyJSON offers dynamic JSON access; Codable is the usual choice on new Swift code.

items.title: Protocol Buffers
items.description: Binary schema-based serialisation for APIs and storage. Google ships protobuf-kotlin-lite for Android; Apple maintains swift-protobuf; Dart and JavaScript have maintained runtimes.

items.title: Dependency injection (graph / container)
items.description: Hilt (built on Dagger) validates the dependency graph at build time via annotation processing. Swinject is a runtime container with no compile-time graph checking. injectable generates get_it registrations in Flutter.

flutter.name: injectable
flutter.install: flutter pub add injectable dev:injectable_generator dev:build_runner

builtin.react_native: No DI container is idiomatic; React Context and module imports cover most cases

items.title: Lightweight DI / service locator
items.description: Koin is a Kotlin DSL (service-locator style, no codegen required). Factory provides property-wrapper based registration in Swift; swift-dependencies from Point-Free is a popular alternative with built-in test overrides. get_it is the common Flutter service locator.

items.title: Local database (object/ORM layer)
items.description: SQLite-backed (Room, drift) or platform-managed (SwiftData, which sits on Core Data) persistence with typed models and observable queries. SwiftData requires iOS 17+; on earlier iOS versions use Core Data or GRDB.

flutter.name: drift
flutter.install: flutter pub add drift dev:drift_dev dev:build_runner

builtin.ios: SwiftData (iOS 17+) and Core Data (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata) are part of the OS

items.title: SQL-first database access
items.description: Write SQL (or thin query builders) and get typed results. SQLDelight generates Kotlin from .sq files; GRDB is a Swift SQLite toolkit with record types and observation; sqflite and expo-sqlite give direct SQLite access.

items.title: Embedded object database (ObjectBox)
items.description: ObjectBox is a non-SQL embedded object database with SDKs for Android/JVM, Swift and Dart.

items.title: Realm database (MongoDB)
items.description: Object database with SDKs on every platform. MongoDB deprecated the Atlas Device SDKs (including Realm and Device Sync) in September 2024 and, per its deprecation page, they reached end-of-life on 2025-09-30. The open-source repositories remain and local-only use works (Realm Kotlin 3.0+ drops sync), but new projects should weigh the lack of vendor-backed development.

items.title: Key-value preferences storage
items.description: Small settings and flags. DataStore replaces SharedPreferences with async, transactional APIs; UserDefaults is the iOS equivalent. Not for secrets (see secure storage).

builtin.android: SharedPreferences (platform API) still works but DataStore is the Jetpack recommendation
builtin.ios: UserDefaults is part of Foundation

items.title: Fast memory-mapped key-value store (MMKV)
items.description: Tencent's mmap-based key-value store, available as a native library on Android and iOS with wrappers for Flutter and React Native.

ios.name: MMKV (iOS)
ios.install: https://github.com/Tencent/MMKV (CocoaPods: pod 'MMKV'; SwiftPM manifest in repo)

items.title: Secure credential storage (Keystore / Keychain)
items.description: Store tokens and secrets in hardware-backed storage. Jetpack Security (EncryptedSharedPreferences / EncryptedFile) is deprecated: its release notes state all APIs are deprecated in favour of platform APIs and direct Android Keystore use. KeychainAccess is a Swift wrapper over Keychain Services (no commits after May 2024 when checked; the raw Keychain API still works). Flutter and React Native wrappers use Keystore and Keychain underneath.

builtin.ios: Keychain Services (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/keychain-services) - platform API

items.title: Cryptography primitives
items.description: Encryption, hashing and signatures. Tink is Google's multi-language crypto library; CryptoKit (Apple, built in) is the standard on iOS, and swift-crypto offers a portable API-compatible implementation.

builtin.ios: CryptoKit (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cryptokit) is part of the OS
builtin.android: javax.crypto / Android Keystore are platform APIs

items.title: Structured concurrency (async/await)
items.description: Kotlin coroutines come from kotlinx.coroutines; Swift Concurrency (async/await, actors, Task) is part of the language and runtime. Dart and JavaScript have Future/Promise with async/await built in.

builtin.ios: Built into the Swift language and runtime

items.title: Observable streams of values (first-party)
items.description: Kotlin Flow/StateFlow (kotlinx.coroutines) versus Combine publishers and AsyncSequence/AsyncStream on Apple platforms. Dart's Stream is built in. For SwiftUI state, the Observation framework (iOS 17+) replaces most Combine ObservableObject use.

builtin.ios: Combine (iOS 13+) and AsyncSequence are built in

items.title: ReactiveX libraries
items.description: The Rx family has a port for each platform. RxJava/RxSwift are common in older codebases; new Android code usually prefers Flow and new Swift code prefers Swift Concurrency or Combine.

items.title: View/screen state holder
items.description: Holds screen state outside the view. Jetpack ViewModel survives configuration changes; Observation's @Observable is the SwiftUI default on iOS 17+. Flutter's provider and React Native's zustand are widely used lightweight options.

builtin.ios: Observation is built in (iOS 17+); ObservableObject on earlier versions

items.title: Unidirectional-data-flow (MVI) frameworks
items.description: Orbit MVI is a Kotlin MVI library with a ViewModel integration; The Composable Architecture (TCA) is Point-Free's Swift equivalent; flutter_bloc and Redux Toolkit are the common Flutter and React Native choices.

items.title: In-app navigation / back stack
items.description: Navigation 3 is the Compose-first Jetpack Navigation library, built around a developer-owned back stack. NavigationStack is SwiftUI's built-in. go_router and React Navigation are the established Flutter and React Native routers.

builtin.ios: NavigationStack is part of SwiftUI (iOS 16+); UINavigationController for UIKit

items.title: Typed / file-based routing
items.description: Navigation Compose supports type-safe routes using serializable classes. swift-navigation (Point-Free) adds state-driven navigation helpers for SwiftUI/UIKit. Expo Router is file-system routing on top of React Navigation.

items.title: Fragment-based navigation component (Views)
items.description: Legacy Android Views navigation graph. UIKit's equivalent is UINavigationController plus coordinators, which is a pattern rather than a library.

builtin.ios: UINavigationController is part of UIKit

items.title: Logging
items.description: Timber adds pluggable trees over android.util.Log; swift-log is Apple's logging API with swappable backends; the OS unified logger (os.Logger) is built in on iOS.

builtin.ios: os.Logger / OSLog (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/os/logger)

items.title: Log destinations (file, remote)
items.description: CocoaLumberjack provides file/remote log destinations on iOS. On Android the usual route is a custom Timber Tree writing to a file or crash reporter.

items.title: In-app network inspector
items.description: Shows captured HTTP traffic inside the debug build. Chucker plugs into OkHttp as an interceptor; Pulse captures URLSession traffic and logs.

items.title: Memory leak detection
items.description: LeakCanary watches for leaked objects in debug builds. On iOS the equivalent workflow is Xcode's Memory Graph Debugger / Instruments (tooling, not a dependency); Flutter's leak_tracker detects leaked Dart objects.

builtin.ios: Memory Graph Debugger and Instruments Leaks are part of Xcode

items.title: Product analytics (Firebase / Google Analytics)
items.description: Event analytics and audiences via Google Analytics for Firebase. Android uses the Firebase BoM; iOS uses the firebase-ios-sdk Swift package (product FirebaseAnalytics).

items.title: Crash reporting (Firebase Crashlytics)
items.description: Real-time crash and non-fatal reporting. Needs the Crashlytics Gradle plugin on Android and a dSYM upload step on iOS.

items.title: Error monitoring & tracing (Sentry)
items.description: Crash and error reporting with performance tracing; first-party SDKs on all four platforms.

items.title: App performance monitoring (Firebase Performance)
items.description: Automatic startup, screen-rendering and network traces plus custom traces.

items.title: Product analytics & feature flags (PostHog)
items.description: Open-source product analytics with session replay and feature flags; first-party SDKs for all four platforms.

items.title: Product analytics (Amplitude)
items.description: Event analytics with Kotlin, Swift, Flutter and React Native SDKs.

items.title: Hosted user authentication (Firebase Auth)
items.description: Email/password, phone, and federated sign-in with Firebase-issued tokens.

items.title: Cloud document database (Cloud Firestore)
items.description: Offline-capable document database with real-time listeners.

items.title: Postgres backend (Supabase)
items.description: Open-source Postgres backend with auth, storage and realtime. Android uses the community supabase-kt (Kotlin Multiplatform); the Swift, Dart and JS clients are published by Supabase.

items.title: Remote push notifications
items.description: Android receives remote push via Firebase Cloud Messaging. iOS delivery always goes through APNs; the Firebase SDK can wrap APNs tokens so one FCM backend serves both. Both platforms require a user-granted notification permission (Android 13+ and iOS).

builtin.ios: APNs registration is built in via UIApplication + UserNotifications (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/registering-your-app-with-apns)

items.title: Push notification service (OneSignal)
items.description: Third-party push/in-app messaging platform with native SDKs.

items.title: Local / scheduled notifications
items.description: Android posts notifications through NotificationManager on a notification channel; iOS schedules UNNotificationRequest via UserNotifications. Notifee (React Native) is archived and no longer maintained; its README recommends expo-notifications.

builtin.android: NotificationManager is part of the platform SDK; NotificationManagerCompat is in androidx.core
builtin.ios: UserNotifications is part of the OS

items.title: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC client (AppAuth)
items.description: OpenID Foundation's AppAuth libraries implement the OAuth 2.0 native-app best-practice (system browser + PKCE) on Android and iOS, with wrappers for Flutter and React Native.

builtin.ios: ASWebAuthenticationSession (AuthenticationServices) is the built-in browser-auth primitive

items.title: Passkeys & credential APIs
items.description: Credential Manager is Android's unified API for passkeys, passwords and federated sign-in. On iOS, passkeys and Sign in with Apple are exposed through AuthenticationServices.

builtin.ios: AuthenticationServices is part of the OS

items.title: Sign in with Google
items.description: On Android, the Google ID helper library (googleid) is used with Credential Manager; the legacy Google Sign-In APIs are being replaced by it. iOS uses the GoogleSignIn-iOS SDK.

items.title: Biometric authentication
items.description: Face/fingerprint prompts. androidx.biometric wraps BiometricPrompt; iOS uses LocalAuthentication (LAContext).

builtin.ios: LocalAuthentication is part of the OS

items.title: App / device attestation
items.description: Prove requests come from a genuine app on a genuine device. Play Integrity (Android) and App Attest/DeviceCheck (iOS) are the platform services; Firebase App Check wraps both for Flutter and React Native.

builtin.ios: DeviceCheck / App Attest are part of the OS

items.title: Image manipulation (resize, crop, rotate, EXIF)
items.description: ExifInterface reads and writes EXIF metadata on Android; ImageIO and Core Image are the iOS frameworks. The Dart image package is pure Dart; expo-image-manipulator wraps native resize/crop for React Native.

builtin.android: android.graphics.Bitmap and BitmapFactory are platform APIs
builtin.ios: ImageIO and Core Image are part of the OS

items.title: Unit-test framework
items.description: JUnit 5 requires an additional Gradle plugin for Android local tests (the AGP default runner is JUnit 4). Swift Testing (Xcode 16+) is the modern Swift framework; XCTest remains for UI and performance tests.

flutter.name: flutter_test
flutter.install: flutter_test (SDK package, included in new Flutter projects)

builtin.ios: XCTest (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xctest) and Swift Testing ship with Xcode

items.title: Mocking
items.description: MockK is a Kotlin-native mocking library. Swift lacks runtime mocking, so tools generate mocks from protocols (Mockolo); mocktail avoids codegen in Dart; Jest has built-in mock functions.

ios.name: Mockolo
ios.install: https://github.com/uber/mockolo (command-line tool; build from source or Homebrew)

builtin.react_native: jest.fn() and jest.mock() are built into Jest

items.title: Testing streams and async code
items.description: Turbine provides a test DSL for Kotlin Flow. In Swift, async/await tests are supported directly by Swift Testing and XCTest.

builtin.ios: Built into XCTest and Swift Testing

items.title: Fluent assertions & matchers
items.description: Truth is Google's fluent assertion library for Java/Kotlin; Nimble provides matchers for Swift tests; Dart and Jest ship matchers in the framework.

items.title: UI / end-to-end test framework (in-process)
items.description: Espresso drives Views on a device/emulator; XCUITest drives the iOS UI out of process; Flutter's integration_test and Detox (React Native) run on device/simulator.

builtin.ios: XCUITest ships with Xcode

items.title: Component / widget UI tests
items.description: Compose's test rule runs UI tests with semantics matchers; Flutter widget tests and React Native Testing Library run without a device. ViewInspector introspects SwiftUI view hierarchies in unit tests.

items.title: Android framework tests on the JVM (Robolectric)
items.description: Robolectric runs Android framework code on a local JVM without an emulator. iOS has no equivalent concept: XCTest runs in the Simulator or, for Swift packages, on the macOS host. Flutter and Jest tests run on the host VM / Node.

ios.name: No direct equivalent: XCTest in Simulator / swift test on host

items.title: Screenshot / snapshot testing
items.description: Paparazzi renders Android Views/Compose on the JVM and diffs against recorded images. swift-snapshot-testing records snapshots of views and other values. Flutter has golden files; Jest has snapshot matchers.

items.title: Cross-platform black-box UI flows (Maestro)
items.description: Maestro runs YAML-defined UI flows against apps on emulators, simulators or devices, independent of the app's UI framework. Same tool on all four platforms.

items.title: HTTP mocking / stubbing in tests
items.description: MockWebServer runs a local server that replays canned responses. OHHTTPStubs intercepts URLSession requests (its repository had no commits after May 2024 when checked). http_mock_adapter does the same for dio; MSW intercepts requests in JavaScript tests.

items.title: Dependency / package manager
items.description: Gradle (with Maven Central and Google Maven), Swift Package Manager (Xcode-integrated), pub for Dart/Flutter, and npm/yarn/pnpm for React Native. CocoaPods remains in many iOS projects, but its maintainers have announced a plan to make the Trunk specs repo read-only (see the CocoaPods blog post 'CocoaPods Trunk Read-only Plan'); prefer SwiftPM for new dependencies.

builtin.ios: SwiftPM is integrated into Xcode; CocoaPods (https://cocoapods.org) and Carthage are external tools
builtin.react_native: yarn (https://yarnpkg.com/) and pnpm (https://pnpm.io/) are common alternatives to npm

items.title: Central dependency versions & lockfiles
items.description: Gradle version catalogs (libs.versions.toml) centralise coordinates and versions. SwiftPM records resolved versions in Package.resolved; Dart in pubspec.lock; npm in package-lock.json.

items.title: Package registries
items.description: Where dependencies are published. Android resolves from Google Maven and Maven Central (JitPack for Git-built libraries); Swift packages resolve from Git URLs, indexed by the Swift Package Index; Dart uses pub.dev; JavaScript uses the npm registry.

items.title: Build system / bundler
items.description: Android Gradle Plugin builds APKs/AABs; Xcode's build system (xcodebuild) builds iOS apps; the Flutter tool drives both; Metro bundles React Native JavaScript.

builtin.ios: Ships with Xcode

items.title: Release automation (fastlane)
items.description: fastlane automates building, signing, screenshots and store uploads for both stores; the same tool is used from Flutter and React Native projects.

android.name: fastlane
android.install: gem install fastlane (or brew install fastlane)

ios.name: fastlane
ios.install: gem install fastlane (or brew install fastlane)

react_native.name: fastlane
react_native.install: gem install fastlane (or brew install fastlane)

flutter.name: fastlane
flutter.install: gem install fastlane (or brew install fastlane)

items.title: Annotation / macro processing
items.description: KSP is Kotlin's symbol-processing API (used by Room, Moshi, Hilt and others). Swift macros (swift-syntax) expand code at compile time. Flutter uses build_runner generators; React Native relies on Babel plugins and TypeScript rather than codegen.

items.title: OpenAPI client generation
items.description: Generate typed API clients from an OpenAPI spec. OpenAPI Generator has Gradle and Dart targets; Apple's swift-openapi-generator is a SwiftPM plugin; orval generates TypeScript clients.

items.title: Typed resource accessors
items.description: AGP generates the R class for resources automatically. Xcode 15+ generates typed symbols for asset catalogs; SwiftGen is the older third-party route and also covers strings and other resources. flutter_gen generates asset constants.

ios.name: SwiftGen
ios.install: https://github.com/SwiftGen/SwiftGen (Homebrew: brew install swiftgen, or SwiftPM plugin)

builtin.android: Built into the Android Gradle Plugin
builtin.ios: Xcode generates asset-catalog symbols (Xcode 15+)

items.title: On-device model runtime
items.description: LiteRT (formerly TensorFlow Lite) runs .tflite models on Android; Core ML is Apple's runtime. Flutter and React Native bindings wrap TFLite.

builtin.ios: Core ML is part of the OS

items.title: Text recognition (OCR)
items.description: ML Kit Text Recognition on Android; Vision's VNRecognizeTextRequest on iOS. Community plugins wrap ML Kit for Flutter and React Native.

builtin.ios: Vision is part of the OS

items.title: Face detection
items.description: ML Kit Face Detection on Android; Vision face-rectangle/landmark requests on iOS.

builtin.ios: Vision is part of the OS

items.title: On-device translation
items.description: ML Kit Translation downloads language models to the device. Apple's Translation framework (iOS 18+ for the programmatic TranslationSession API) provides system translation.

builtin.ios: Translation is part of the OS

items.title: On-device generative AI
items.description: ML Kit GenAI APIs (such as the Prompt API) expose Gemini Nano on supported Android devices; Apple's Foundation Models framework exposes the on-device model on Apple Intelligence devices (iOS 26+). Both depend on device and OS support. LiteRT-LM (com.google.ai.edge.litertlm) runs open models on Android.

builtin.ios: Foundation Models is part of the OS (iOS 26+, Apple Intelligence-capable devices)

items.title: Speech recognition
items.description: Android's SpeechRecognizer and Apple's Speech framework provide platform speech-to-text; plugins wrap them for Flutter and React Native. The older @react-native-voice/voice package is marked deprecated on npm in favour of expo-speech-recognition.

builtin.android: SpeechRecognizer is part of the platform SDK
builtin.ios: Speech is part of the OS

items.title: Text-to-speech
items.description: Android TextToSpeech and iOS AVSpeechSynthesizer are platform APIs; flutter_tts and expo-speech wrap them.

builtin.android: TextToSpeech is part of the platform SDK
builtin.ios: AVSpeechSynthesizer is part of the OS

items.title: Camera capture
items.description: CameraX provides lifecycle-aware preview, capture, analysis and video; AVFoundation's capture APIs (AVCaptureSession) are the iOS counterpart. VisionCamera is the community React Native standard; Flutter's camera plugin is maintained by the Flutter team.

builtin.ios: AVFoundation is part of the OS

items.title: Audio / video playback
items.description: Media3 ExoPlayer on Android; AVPlayer/AVKit on iOS. video_player is the Flutter team's plugin; react-native-video is the common React Native player.

builtin.ios: AVFoundation / AVKit are part of the OS

items.title: Background playback & media session
items.description: Media3 MediaSession/MediaSessionService exposes playback to the system (lock screen, Bluetooth, Android Auto). MPNowPlayingInfoCenter and MPRemoteCommandCenter do this on iOS. audio_service and react-native-track-player package it for Flutter and React Native.

builtin.ios: MediaPlayer framework is part of the OS

items.title: Photo / media picker
items.description: The Android Photo Picker (ActivityResultContracts.PickVisualMedia) and iOS PHPickerViewController both let users share selected media without broad storage/photo-library permission.

builtin.ios: PhotosUI is part of the OS

items.title: In-app purchases (store billing APIs)
items.description: Google Play Billing Library on Android; StoreKit 2 on iOS (async/await API, iOS 15+). Flutter's in_app_purchase wraps both. react-native-iap moved to the OpenIAP monorepo; its old GitHub repo is archived but the npm package is still published.

builtin.ios: StoreKit is part of the OS

items.title: Subscription management platform (RevenueCat)
items.description: RevenueCat wraps Play Billing and StoreKit behind one SDK and backend; first-party SDKs on all four platforms.

items.title: In-app review prompt
items.description: Ask for a store rating without leaving the app. The OS decides whether the prompt actually appears on both platforms.

builtin.ios: StoreKit is part of the OS

items.title: Device location
items.description: Fused Location Provider (Google Play services) on Android; Core Location on iOS. Both require runtime permission. geolocator and expo-location wrap them for Flutter and React Native.

builtin.android: android.location.LocationManager is the platform API (no Play services needed)
builtin.ios: Core Location is part of the OS

items.title: Map view SDK
items.description: Google Maps SDK / Maps Compose on Android; MapKit on iOS (SwiftUI Map). Flutter and React Native have well-known wrappers over the native SDKs.

builtin.ios: MapKit is part of the OS

items.title: Health & fitness data
items.description: Health Connect (Android) and HealthKit (iOS) both require explicit per-data-type permissions. The Flutter `health` plugin covers both; React Native splits into platform-specific libraries.

builtin.ios: HealthKit is part of the OS

items.title: Bluetooth Low Energy
items.description: Nordic's Android-BLE-Library wraps BluetoothGatt; CoreBluetooth is the iOS framework. flutter_blue_plus and react-native-ble-plx cover both platforms.

builtin.ios: CoreBluetooth is part of the OS

items.title: Deferrable background work
items.description: WorkManager on Android; BGTaskScheduler on iOS. Both let the OS decide when to run; iOS is far more restrictive and gives no guarantee of timing.

builtin.ios: BackgroundTasks is part of the OS

items.title: Remote config
items.description: Server-controlled parameters fetched at runtime. Firebase Remote Config has SDKs on all four platforms.

items.title: Vendor-neutral feature flags (OpenFeature)
items.description: OpenFeature is a CNCF specification with provider-based SDKs. SDKs exist for Kotlin (Android) and Swift (the Kotlin SDK is pre-1.0). Other languages have their own SDKs that are not listed here.

items.title: Firebase Dynamic Links (shut down)
items.description: Firebase Dynamic Links stopped serving links on 2025-08-25 per Firebase's deprecation FAQ. Migrate to App Links / Universal Links (see the Equivalents page) or a deep-link provider.

ios.name: Firebase Dynamic Links (iOS)
ios.install: https://github.com/firebase/firebase-ios-sdk - product FirebaseDynamicLinks (do not use in new code)

items.title: Date & time API
items.description: Android API 26+ has java.time natively; core library desugaring (desugar_jdk_libs) backports it to older API levels. Foundation's Date, Calendar and DateFormatter (or Date.FormatStyle) are the iOS APIs. intl handles formatting in Dart; date-fns is a common utility in JavaScript.

builtin.android: java.time is built in on API 26+
builtin.ios: Foundation is part of the OS
builtin.react_native: Date and Intl.DateTimeFormat are built in (Hermes)

items.title: Multiplatform date-time (kotlinx-datetime)
items.description: A Kotlin Multiplatform date/time library with the same API on Android and iOS. Native Swift code simply uses Foundation.

builtin.ios: Foundation is part of the OS

items.title: Runtime permission requests
items.description: Android: the first-party Activity Result API (ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission); Accompanist Permissions adds Compose state helpers. iOS has no single API: each framework requests its own authorisation. permission_handler and react-native-permissions unify them.

builtin.ios: Each framework (CoreLocation, AVFoundation, Photos, ...) provides its own request API; Info.plist usage strings are mandatory

items.title: In-app browser / web auth tab
items.description: Custom Tabs (Android) and SFSafariViewController / ASWebAuthenticationSession (iOS) open web content in a system-managed browser UI.

builtin.ios: SafariServices is part of the OS

items.title: Static analysis / linter
items.description: detekt is a Kotlin static analyzer (the coordinate shown is the latest stable 1.x line; the 2.x alphas publish under dev.detekt). Android Lint also ships with AGP for Android-specific checks. SwiftLint enforces Swift style and conventions. Dart's analyzer uses flutter_lints; ESLint covers TypeScript/JavaScript.

ios.name: SwiftLint
ios.install: https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint (Homebrew: brew install swiftlint, or SwiftPM plugin)

builtin.android: Android Lint (https://developer.android.com/studio/write/lint) ships with the Android Gradle Plugin
builtin.flutter: dart analyze ships with the Dart SDK

items.title: Code formatter
items.description: ktlint formats and lints Kotlin to the official style (Spotless is a Gradle wrapper that can run it). SwiftFormat reformats Swift. dart format is built in; Prettier is the JavaScript standard.

builtin.flutter: dart format ships with the Dart SDK

items.title: Immutable / persistent collections
items.description: kotlinx-collections-immutable provides persistent lists/maps (and stable types for Compose). Swift value semantics make most collections effectively immutable; swift-collections adds extra data structures. built_collection and immer fill the role in Dart and JavaScript.
